2026-11-09
Switched to a new branch 'alee/positioning-retire-only-tool-claims'
(`codegraph_explore`).

**The sharpening this forced.** "archy checks the part you cannot see" is not
quite true and codegraph is why: ask it the right question and it *will* show
you that `models` imports `repositories`. What it will not do is say so
unprompted, call it wrong, or fail a build. The honest line is not visibility,
it is **assertion**: descriptive tools answer questions, archy makes a claim
that breaks CI. The README now says it that way.

### 3b. The risk this analysis previously left as comfort

**The moat is product intent, not capability, and that should be written down
rather than assumed.** codegraph already holds the graph. Tarjan's algorithm is
textbook, and a rules config is a weekend's work. If enforcement ever serves
their job, the technical barrier is approximately zero and the distribution gap
(62.8k stars against 5) means they would arrive with an audience archy does not
have.

What protects archy today is that enforcement does not serve navigation and
token reduction, which is the job they have measurably chosen (a reported 60%
cost reduction across seven benchmark repos). That is a real and durable reason,
----
codegraph already dominates (§2). So the finding is not "archy should go
symbol-level"; it is **archy should stop competing where symbol granularity is
the deciding factor**.

Cost note, recorded so a future revisit starts correctly: archy's graph is
**internal-only by construction** (`_external_target` collapses external nodes,
`assemble_graph` drops external edges), and `PATTERN_DETECTION_EMPIRICS.md`
already found that any analysis needing external imports has to reach one layer
below the graph. A symbol-level rebuild would be a bigger change than that, not
a smaller one: new node type through graph, index, cache, every tool, and the
score.

## 6. C3: the one falsifiable sentence

> **archy is the only local, agent-facing tool that holds a codebase's
> *declared* structure (layers, forbidden edges, an acyclicity invariant, a
> recorded score baseline) and reports when an edit or a week of edits violates
> it; every graph tool in its category, codegraph included, describes the
> structure that exists and has no representation of the structure you
> intended.**

Falsifiable three ways, and worth re-checking on any revisit:

1. codegraph (or an equivalent) ships architecture rules, a quality score, or a
   trend. Today: none of the three.
2. import-linter, deptry, or a similar Python tool ships an agent-facing MCP
   surface with a composite score and history. import-linter is the closest
   (archy *wraps* it for transitive contracts) but is CI-shaped, not
   agent-shaped, and has no score.
3. Someone demonstrates that the normative job does not need a tool, because an
   agent reading `archy.yaml` plus `CLAUDE.md` complies just as well.
   **Partially true already**, and recorded in
   [`FUTURE.md`](../FUTURE.md): the 2026-05 agent-loop test in
   `governingdocs/backend` found a fresh agent caught a forbidden cross-layer
   import by *reading the config*, not by calling `archy_check`. This is the
   most dangerous of the three and the one archy has the least evidence
   against.

## 7. Is archy worth working on? (C3, the part the ticket actually cares about)

Separate two questions that keep getting merged.

**Is archy differentiated? Yes, and more cleanly than expected.** 11 of 13 MCP
tools have no counterpart in the most successful tool in the adjacent category. The
normative job is real, unoccupied, and structurally hard for a
navigation-first tool to enter, because it needs user-supplied intent rather
----

  src/archy/cli.py:82: archy.cli -> archy.headers  (line: 82)
  src/archy/cli.py:87: archy.cli -> archy.impact  (line: 87)
  src/archy/cli.py:1537: archy.cli -> archy.index  (lines: 1537, 1538, 1566, 1591)
  src/archy/cli.py:1511: archy.cli -> archy.mcp  (line: 1511)
  src/archy/cli.py:111: archy.cli -> archy.scan_config  (line: 111)
  src/archy/cli.py:113: archy.cli -> archy.simulate  (line: 113)
  src/archy/conventions.py:72: archy.conventions -> archy.graph  (line: 72)
  src/archy/duplicates.py:84: archy.duplicates -> archy.graph  (line: 84)
  src/archy/graph.py:40: archy.graph -> archy.cli  (line: 40)
  src/archy/headers.py:44: archy.headers -> archy.conventions  (line: 44)
  src/archy/headers.py:45: archy.headers -> archy.graph  (line: 45)
  src/archy/impact.py:28: archy.impact -> archy.graph  (line: 28)
  src/archy/index.py:31: archy.index -> archy.graph  (line: 31)
  src/archy/mcp.py:117: archy.mcp -> archy.affected  (line: 117)
----
**7. Commercial / enterprise.** Different buyer, similar idea.
- [CodeScene](https://codescene.com/product/code-health) - `CodeHealth` score, behavior-aware (combines git history with code). Strongest commercial story for "single trended health metric."
- [Structure101](https://structure101.com/) (acquired by Sonar) - tangles + excessive complexity as TD measures.
- Sonargraph, NDepend (.NET), Lattix - DSM-based architectural analysis, enterprise pricing.

### What this implies for archy's design

The only tools sharing **all** of {Python-native, import-graph, layer rules, trended score, MCP server} are archy and the generic Claude Code `architect` plugin. Cross-referenced against the most-cited competitors:

| Capability | archy | sentrux | tach | import-linter | pytest-archon | CodeScene |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Python-deep (transitive contracts) | ✅ | ❌ | partial | ✅ | partial | ❌ |
| Multi-language | ❌ | ✅ (52) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |

https://github.com/hslee16/Archy/pull/862
docs(skill,mcp): drop the unmeasured "consult archy on each edit" cadence and the "cheap" claim
documentation
**The gap.** Four agent-facing surfaces tell agents to call archy around every edit, justified by calls being "cheap":
- `_AGENT_LOOP_PROMPT`, `src/archy/mcp.py:199-200`: "makes every call cheap ... so consult archy on *each* edit".
- `skills/archy/SKILL.md:18` (and the byte-identical `plugins/claude/skills/archy/SKILL.md`): "Consult archy on *each* edit ... impact before, diff after".
- `SKILL.md:193`: `archy_diff` "After every edit".
- `docs/AGENT_LOOP.md:10-13`.

Nothing archy has measured supports a per-edit cadence, and "cheap" rests on wall-clock latency, not tokens. The skill also contradicts itself: `SKILL.md:51` (added by #475) puts verification after the edit, alongside the tests.

**What this is, and is not.** Claims hygiene, same precedent as #304. It is not a behaviour intervention, and the PR must not claim one:
- Agents already mostly ignore the instruction (archy fired in 84 of 132 Study 8 runs, median zero calls before the first edit), so removing it will change little of what agents do.
- None of the six delivery nulls measured per-edit pull cadence, and the external sources (arXiv 2608.13568, an LSP localization study that calls itself preliminary; local-code-navigator, which attributes its context cost to tool schemas loading every turn) do not either. Do not cite them as evidence for the new wording.
- "Call at verification points" is unmeasured too. Present it as the step whose verdict can block a commit, not as a better cadence.

**Anti-theater.** The guidance stops asserting a benefit archy cannot show and stops contradicting itself. That is the whole change.

**Fix.**
1. Remove "consult archy on *each* edit (impact before, diff after)" and "After every edit".
2. Replace "cheap" with "fast" (warm builds take seconds); make no token claim.
3. Align with the `SKILL.md:51` framing: discovery is `rg`, navigation is archy once a module is named, verification is `archy_diff` / `archy_check` / `cycles --strict` before commit, at the end of a task, and when an edit adds or removes a cross-package import. Describe the loop as optional.
4. Copy the skill to the plugin mirror (`tests/test_plugin.py:68` requires byte equality).

Leave `src/archy/install/base.py` alone: its rules text already says "after edits, call archy_diff", not a per-edit cadence, and changing it would mean regenerating the syrupy snapshots in `tests/install/snapshot`.

**Acceptance.**
- A grep across `src/`, `skills/`, `plugins/` and `docs/` (excluding `docs/WHAT_DIDNT_WORK.md`) finds no "each* edit", "every edit" or "every call cheap".
- The plugin mirror test and the MCP loop-prompt registration test pass.
- The full CI set is green (`ruff check` with no path, `ruff format --check`, `ty`, `pytest`, `archy check`, `archy cycles --strict`, `conventions --emit-headers --check`).

**Sources.** archy's own delivery-line table: `docs/WHAT_DIDNT_WORK.md`. Context only, not evidence for the change: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13568 , https://github.com/vkuprin/local-code-navigator .

Found by an adversarially-vetted research loop (two independent refuting reviewers per proposal).

Base directory for this skill: /Users/hosanglee/.claude/plugins/cache/deepwork-plugins/deepwork/0.14.0/skills/review

# DeepWork Review

Run automated code reviews on the current branch based on `.deepreview` config files.

## Routing — Check Before Proceeding

**STOP and redirect** if either of these applies:

- User wants to **configure, create, or modify** review rules (e.g., "add a security review", "set up reviews for our API layer") → use the `configure_reviews` skill instead
- User wants to **add a doc-sync rule** (keep a documentation file in sync with source files) → call `start_workflow` with `job_name="deepwork_reviews"` and `workflow_name="add_document_update_rule"`

Only proceed past this section if the user wants to **run** reviews.

## Pre-flight — Verify Agent Availability

Before running reviews, check that the `deepwork:reviewer` agent is available. If it does not appear in the agents list (i.e., the Agent tool does not list `deepwork:reviewer` as a valid `subagent_type`), **STOP** and tell the user:

> The `deepwork:reviewer` agent is not available. Please run `/reload-plugins` to pick up the latest plugin updates, then try again.

Do not proceed with reviews until the agent is available.

## How to Run

1. Call the `mcp__deepwork__get_review_instructions` tool directly:
   - **No arguments** to review the current branch's changes (auto-detects via git diff against the main branch).
   - **With `files`** to review only specific files: `mcp__deepwork__get_review_instructions(files=["src/app.py", "src/lib.py"])`. When provided, only reviews whose include/exclude patterns match the given files will be returned. Use this when the user asks to review a particular file or set of files rather than the whole branch.
   - **If the result says no rules are configured**: Ask the user if they'd like to auto-discover and set up rules. If yes, invoke the `/deepwork` skill with the `deepwork_reviews` job's `discover_rules` workflow. Stop here — do not proceed with running reviews if there are no rules.
2. The output will list review tasks to invoke in parallel. Each task has `description`, `subagent_type`, and `prompt` fields — these map directly to the Agent tool parameters. Launch all of them as parallel agents.
3. **While review agents run**, check for a changelog and open PR (see below).
4. Collect the results from all review agents.

## Changelog & PR Description Check

Run this concurrently with the review agents (step 2 above) — don't wait for reviews to finish first.

1. Check if the project has a changelog file (e.g., `CHANGELOG.md`, `CHANGELOG`, `CHANGES.md`).
2. If a changelog exists and there are commits on the current branch beyond the main branch:
   - Read the changelog and the branch's commit log (`git log main..HEAD --oneline`).
   - Verify the changelog's unreleased/current section accurately reflects what the branch does. If entries are missing, outdated, or inaccurate, update the changelog.
3. If a PR is open for the current branch (check with `gh pr view`):
   - If you updated the changelog, also verify the PR description matches. Update it with `gh pr edit` if needed.
   - If the changelog was already accurate, skip the PR description check.

## Acting on Results

For each finding from the review agents:

- **Obviously good changes with no downsides** (e.g., fixing a typo, removing an unused import, adding a missing null check): make the change immediately without asking. When in doubt, ask.
- **Everything else** (refactors, style changes, architectural suggestions, anything with trade-offs):
  1. Use AskUserQuestion to ask the user about each finding **individually**. Do not group issues together unless they are the same issue occurring in multiple files; otherwise, use AskUserQuestion to ask about each issue separately. This lets the user make separate decisions on each item.
  2. For each question, provide several concrete fix approaches as options when there are reasonable alternatives (e.g., "Update the spec to match the code" vs "Update the code to match the spec" vs "Skip").
  3. If a finding seems minor or debatable, include an option to suppress that error in the future — such as a clarification to the rule if it is too narrow, or a comment on the offending content if comments work in that context.
  4. Be concise — quote the key finding, don't dump the full review.

When a finding is dismissed (user chooses "Skip" or you determine it's not actionable for this PR), call `mcp__deepwork__mark_review_as_passed` with the review's ID so it won't re-run on subsequent iterations.

## Iterate

After making any changes:

1. Call `mcp__deepwork__get_review_instructions` with `files` set to **only the files you edited** during this iteration. This scopes the re-review to your changes rather than re-reviewing the entire branch.
2. Repeat the cycle (run → act on results → run again) until a clean run — one where all review agents return no findings, or all remaining findings have been explicitly skipped by the user.
3. On subsequent runs, you only need to re-run tasks that had findings last time — skip tasks that were clean.
4. Reviews that already passed are automatically skipped as long as reviewed files remain unchanged.

content.text:
PR #862 for #535 is open and its CI is green, including CodeScene, which left no inline comments. The three DeepWork review agents are still running, so I haven't started #534 yet.

What the PR does:
- **Analysis doc:** it adds a dated section 3c to `docs/research/CODEGRAPH_COMPETITIVE_ANALYSIS.md`. That section records optave/codegraph, agent-arch, and the fact that colbymchenry/codegraph is still rule-free at v1.6.2 (re-checked 2026-11-09). It also marks falsifier 1 as fired and narrows the section 6 claim.
- **README:** the navigation-graph sentence is now scoped to colbymchenry/codegraph, and the README acknowledges that optave/codegraph, tach and agent-arch carry declared boundaries. It also names which codegraph the "sharp version" paragraph is about.
- **LEARNINGS.md:** I left line 245 unchanged. optave is multi-language and agent-arch has no MCP server, so the "all of" conjunction still holds.

Things that differ from the ticket:
- **Line numbers:** README is at 188 and 190, not 145 and 147, so I edited by content.
- **optave push date:** the last push was 2026-11-04, not 2026-10-21.
- **Dropped claims:** optave ships `snapshot.ts` and `branch-compare.ts`, so I did not claim snapshot/diff as unique. I also did not claim a trend, since I couldn't verify it against optave's source. What's left as differences is Python `__init__` re-export resolution, transitive `forbid:` and `required:` reach. I checked `boundaries.ts` for the last two and found neither.
- **tach:** I took the ticket's word that tach carries declared boundaries and did not verify it.

When the review results arrive I'll fix any findings, then start #534 on a fresh branch.

# codegraph vs archy: is Python-only, module-level scope defensible, or a gap?

Answers [#316](https://github.com/hslee16/Archy/issues/316). The benchmark
forensics on [codegraph](https://github.com/colbymchenry/codegraph) are already
closed in [`TOKEN_REDUCTION_CLAIMS.md`](TOKEN_REDUCTION_CLAIMS.md) §8 (task
class, no correctness control) and are not redone here. This document answers
the capability and positioning question instead: **is archy's scope a
deliberate position or a gap, and is archy differentiated enough to keep
building?**

Fact-gathering date: 2026-07-24, with §3a and §3b re-verified against the live
repository on 2026-07-27 after #369 made the descriptive-versus-normative split
archy's headline. Every number below is measured, not asserted; where a number
could not be pulled it says so.

## Summary

**The scope is defensible and the differentiation is real, but it is not the
thing that decides whether archy is worth working on.**

- codegraph and archy do **different jobs**: codegraph is **descriptive**
  (what is in this codebase, where, and what calls what), archy is
  **normative** (what did you declare this codebase should look like, and is it
  drifting). codegraph ships **no quality score, no architecture rules, no
  cycle analysis, no history, and no counterfactual check**. That is not an
  oversight on their part; it is a different product.
- Where the two **do** overlap, archy loses on the merits, and the overlap is
  narrow: 2 of archy's 13 MCP tools (3 CLI commands), and none of the 11 that
  carry its actual thesis.
- **Multi-language: still no** (C1), but the honest reason changed. Not "wrong
  axis"; "the axis where a funded, viral competitor wins and archy would spend
  everything to draw".
- **Module-level: correct** (C2), and not a rationalization. Archy's five axes
  are module and package constructs; four of them are undefined or degenerate
  at symbol granularity.
- **The uncomfortable finding is not about scope at all.** archy has 5 stars,
  3 outside PRs, and an empty `ADOPTERS.md` after 2.5 months. codegraph has
  62,279 stars and 385,293 npm downloads per month after 6. The gap between
  those two numbers is not explained by language coverage or graph
  granularity. It is distribution. **Differentiation is not archy's problem.**

edge dump. Before a non-trivial edit, call
   `archy_what_to_refactor_next(path, lens='structural')` to see whether
   your target sits in the project's central-and-fragile zone (high blast
   radius combined with high instability); if it does, scope down or pause
   for review.

   If the edit changes imports (adds or removes a dependency), call
   `archy_simulate(path, add=[{from, to}], remove=[...])` first: it
   returns the would-be cycles, layer violations, and score delta with
   no file written, so you can abandon or reshape a plan that introduces
   a cycle before touching code instead of catching it in step 4.
3. **Edit** the code as you normally would.
4. **Diff** after the edit to see what got better, what got worse, and
   exactly which cycles or layer rules changed:
   `archy_diff(path)`
5. Read `summary.headline` first - one structured sentence
   ("overall +X; driven by Y; cycles +A/-B"). Then walk
   `summary.top_regressions` in order; each item carries a `risk` score
   (0-1, from `compute_edit_risk`) so the most central/fragile breakage
   surfaces first. The raw `score_delta`, `cycles`, `violations`, and
   `sdp_violations` blocks remain available for when you need the full
   list, but the summary is the right starting point: it's the same
   ranking you would have done by hand. If the headline shows
   `overall -...` or any `top_regressions` exist, inspect the named
   modules, fix or revert, then loop back to step 4. Recurse until the
   diff is clean (empty `top_regressions`).
#####
Archy turns the structural health of a Python codebase into numbers and rule violations an agent can act on between edits. This skill explains when to reach for it and how to drive its MCP tools as a tight feedback loop.

**What it is actually for.** A file tree shows you the layers. It does not show you dependency *direction*, transitive reach, or cycles, and those are where the mistakes land: measured across 25 agent-built backends, every unaided failure produced the four layer directories correctly and then imported upward, entities reaching into data access. Reading the config catches the local, visible cases; the multi-hop ones need the graph. Reach for `archy_check` and `archy_cycles` on direction, and `archy_impact` before an edit crosses modules.

Archy keeps a persistent parse cache (`.archy/index.db`), kept warm by a background file watcher in `archy mcp`, so its tools stay cheap to call: warm graph builds take a few seconds even on 10k+ module repos because only files whose content changed are re-parsed. Lean on that. Consult archy on *each* edit to keep your working surface relevant (impact before, diff after), not only at the start and end of a task. Freshness is automatic (every tool re-syncs changed files on demand, so a result is never stale); the CLI `archy index status` reports the cache state if you ever want to confirm it out of band.

## Prerequisites

Prefer the `archy_*` MCP tools below. The user wires the server up once in their MCP client config:
#####
| `archy_cycles` | `archy cycles . --format json` | `--min-size N`, `--strict` |
| `archy_score` | `archy score . --format json` | `view="history"`: `archy trend . --format json` |
| `archy_dsm` | `archy dsm . --format json` | `--group`, `--focus`, `--package`, `--diff FILE` |
| `archy_duplicates` | `archy duplicates . --format json` | `--near-miss` |
| `archy_conventions` | `archy conventions . --format json` | |
| `archy_module_view` | `archy conventions . --module X --format json` | |
| `archy_brief` | `archy brief . --format json` | `--contracts` |

## When to activate

Activate this skill when any of the following is true:

#####
# Agent feedback loop

archy turns a Python codebase's structural health into a number that an
AI agent can act on between edits, the way sentrux does for Rust. This
doc describes the recommended loop. The same playbook is also exposed
as the `loop` prompt on the MCP server, so an agent connected to
`archy mcp` can pull it on demand.

A persistent parse cache (`.archy/index.db`), kept warm by a background file
watcher inside `archy mcp`, keeps every call cheap: warm graph builds are a
few seconds even on 10k+ module repos, because only files whose content
changed are re-parsed. That economics is the point of the loop below: consult
archy on *each* edit to keep your working surface relevant (impact before,
diff after), not just once at the start and end. Freshness is automatic: every
tool re-syncs changed files on demand, so a result is never stale; the CLI
`archy index status` reports the cache state if you ever want to confirm it
explicitly.

## The loop

![The archy agent loop: six stations, Snapshot, Impact, Risk, Edit, Diff and Fix or revert, arranged clockwise around a shared .archy/baseline.json record that only Snapshot writes and only Diff reads back.](assets/diagrams/agent-loop.png)

Work advances around the ring once per edit; the baseline at the centre is the
only thing that persists across passes, which is why a stale one quietly
invalidates every later diff.

1. **Snapshot** at session start so you have a baseline.

   - CLI: `archy snapshot .`
   - MCP: `archy_snapshot(path)`

#####
Archy turns the structural health of a Python codebase into numbers and rule violations an agent can act on between edits. This skill explains when to reach for it and how to drive its MCP tools as a tight feedback loop.

**What it is actually for.** A file tree shows you the layers. It does not show you dependency *direction*, transitive reach, or cycles, and those are where the mistakes land: measured across 25 agent-built backends, every unaided failure produced the four layer directories correctly and then imported upward, entities reaching into data access. Reading the config catches the local, visible cases; the multi-hop ones need the graph. Reach for `archy_check` and `archy_cycles` on direction, and `archy_impact` before an edit crosses modules.

Archy keeps a persistent parse cache (`.archy/index.db`), kept warm by a background file watcher in `archy mcp`, so its tools stay cheap to call: warm graph builds take a few seconds even on 10k+ module repos because only files whose content changed are re-parsed. Lean on that. Consult archy on *each* edit to keep your working surface relevant (impact before, diff after), not only at the start and end of a task. Freshness is automatic (every tool re-syncs changed files on demand, so a result is never stale); the CLI `archy index status` reports the cache state if you ever want to confirm it out of band.

only thing that persists across passes, which is why a stale one quietly

fix(install): a global install puts archy's "call it before you edit" block in every project's agent instructions
enhancement
**Problem.** `archy install` defaults to `--location global` (`src/archy/cli.py:1615-1617`). On that path every adapter writes the marker-fenced block from `src/archy/install/base.py:79` into a client-wide instruction file: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (adapters/claude.py:74), `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` (adapters/codex.py:47), `~/.cursor/rules/archy.mdc`, the opencode `AGENTS.md`, and `~/.continue/rules/archy.md`. Claude Code and Codex load their global file in every session of every project. The block (about 1,350 characters) tells the agent to "Ask it before you decide", to call `archy_impact` "Before editing", and to "Take a baseline with `archy_snapshot` at the start of a task".

So a user who installs archy for one Python project now has that instruction in their TypeScript, Go and documentation repositories too. Following it there is not harmless. On a scratch repo containing only `src/index.ts`, `archy snapshot` writes `.archy/baseline.json` and prints `score: 1.000  cycles: 0  violations: 0` with exit 0. The agent gets a perfect score for code archy cannot read, plus an untracked file in the user's tree (related: #523).

**Evidence.**
- Instructions in context files are followed, but they do not improve task success and raise inference cost by over 20%, for LLM-generated and developer-written files alike: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11988
- Thoughtworks Radar Vol. 34 puts "agent instruction bloat" on Caution: https://www.thoughtworks.com/radar/techniques
- archy's own delivery line: six interventions, none positive, the last two costing 1.26x and 1.128x their controls (`docs/WHAT_DIDNT_WORK.md`, Study 8).
- Nx's MCP server now defaults to `--minimal` and moves guidance into on-demand skills: https://nx.dev/docs/reference/nx-mcp

None of these measured this block, so this ticket claims no token or cost saving.

**What changes for the user.** `archy install` with the default global location registers the MCP server and seeds the Claude permission allowlist, and writes no instruction block. Running `archy install --location local` inside a Python project still writes the block into that project's `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` / rules file, so the guidance appears only where the user opted archy in. Re-running a global install on a machine that already has the global block removes it.

**Scope.**
- In each adapter's `plan()`, emit the `kind="instructions"` `FileAction` only when `scope == "local"`.
- For a global install, add an action that strips an existing archy block using the existing `remove_instructions` / `delete_file` unrender paths. The user's own text around the markers must stay byte-identical. For files archy owns outright (`rules/archy.mdc`, `rules/archy.md`), delete the file.
- `--print-config <id>` for global shows no instruction file, or shows the removal.
- Update `docs/INSTALL.md` ("What gets installed", item 2, and the path matrix) and README.md:470.
- Regenerate the syrupy snapshots in `tests/install/snapshot`.

**Definition of done.**
- On a fake `HOME`, a test runs a global install for every adapter. `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` are not created when absent, and a pre-existing one with user text is byte-identical afterwards. Mutation-verified: restore the unconditional instructions `FileAction`, clear `__pycache__`, confirm red.
- A migration test: a global file holding user text plus an old archy block comes out as just the user text, byte-identical, after a global install.
- A guard test: a local install still writes the block into the project file, so the fix cannot pass by deleting the block everywhere. Mutation-verified by dropping the local branch.
- Install, then uninstall, still leaves every client file byte-identical (the existing idempotency harness).
- The full CI set is green: `uv run ruff check` (no path), `ruff format --check`, `ty check`, `pytest`, `archy check .`, `archy cycles . --strict`, `archy conventions . --emit-headers --check`.

**Non-goals.**
- No claim that removing the block saves tokens or improves agents. Nothing measured it.
- Not rewording the local block (that wording belongs with #534).
- Not changing MCP tool descriptions or the `loop` prompt.
- No hooks (#132).
- Not making `snapshot` refuse non-Python trees (#523 covers the 0-module clean pass).

From the 2026-10-26 research report.

"""Claude Code adapter.

The richest adapter: besides the MCP stanza it seeds the `permissions.allow`
allowlist the plugin manifest cannot write (the gap surfaced shipping the
plugin in #104), and it skips the MCP write when the archy Claude plugin is
already installed, to avoid the double-registration that produces duplicated
`mcp__archy__*` / `mcp__plugin_archy_archy__*` tools.

Paths:
- global MCP config: ``~/.claude.json`` (`mcpServers` object)
- local MCP config:  ``<project>/.mcp.json`` (Claude Code's project-scope file)
- permissions:       ``~/.claude/settings.json`` / ``<project>/.claude/settings.json``
- instructions:      ``~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`` / ``<project>/CLAUDE.md``

archy:owns        ClaudeAdapter
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

from archy.install import paths
from archy.install.base import (
    AgentAdapter,
    FileAction,
    Scope,
    local_root,
    remove_instructions,
    upsert_instructions,
)
from archy.install.merge import (
    render_claude_permissions,
    render_json_mcp,
    strip_claude_permissions,
    strip_json_mcp,
)


class ClaudeAdapter(AgentAdapter):
    id = "claude"
    name = "Claude Code"
    cli_name = "claude"

    def config_paths(self, scope: Scope, project_root: Path | None = None) -> list[Path]:
        if scope is Scope.LOCAL:
            return [local_root(project_root) / ".mcp.json"]
        return [paths.home() / ".claude.json"]

    def detection_paths(self) -> list[Path]:
        home = paths.home()
        return [home / ".claude.json", home / ".claude"]

    def mac_app_bundles(self) -> list[Path]:
        return [
            Path("/Applications/Claude.app"),
            paths.home() / "Applications" / "Claude.app",
        ]

    def windows_install_dirs(self) -> list[Path]:
        local = paths.local_appdata()
        if local is None:
            return []
        return [local / "AnthropicClaude", local / "Programs" / "Claude"]

    def _permissions_path(self, scope: Scope, project_root: Path | None) -> Path:
        if scope is Scope.LOCAL:
            return local_root(project_root) / ".claude" / "settings.json"
        return paths.home() / ".claude" / "settings.json"

    def _instructions_path(self, scope: Scope, project_root: Path | None) -> Path:
        if scope is Scope.LOCAL:
            return local_root(project_root) / "CLAUDE.md"
        return paths.home() / ".claude" / "CLAUDE.md"

    def plugin_installed(self) -> bool:
        """Heuristic: is the archy Claude plugin already linked into ~/.claude?

        Scans the plugins directory shallowly for a manifest named "archy". If
        the plugin is present it already registers the MCP server and ships the
        skill, so we skip the MCP and instruction writes (but still seed
        permissions, which the plugin cannot). Best-effort: any read error means
        "not installed", since a false negative just risks a redundant stanza
        the user can remove, while a false positive would leave them unwired.
        """
        plugins_dir = paths.home() / ".claude" / "plugins"
        if not plugins_dir.exists():
            return False
        try:
            for manifest in plugins_dir.glob("*/.claude-plugin/plugin.json"):
                try:
                    if json.loads(manifest.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).get("name") == "archy":
                        return True
                except (OSError, ValueError):
                    continue
        except OSError:
            return False
        return False

    def plan(
        self,
        scope: Scope,
        *,
        project_root: Path | None = None,
        seed_permissions: bool = True,
        for_uninstall: bool = False,
    ) -> list[FileAction]:
        actions: list[FileAction] = []
        # On install we skip the MCP + instruction writes when the archy plugin
        # already registers them (avoids the #104 double-registration). On
        # uninstall we must include them unconditionally: a prior install done
        # while the plugin was absent may have written a manual stanza, and
        # gating removal on the *current* plugin state is exactly what left
        # those files orphaned and broke install/uninstall symmetry (#169). The
        # strip/remove operations are idempotent no-ops when nothing is there.
        if for_uninstall or not self.plugin_installed():
            actions.append(
                FileAction(
                    path=self.config_paths(scope, project_root)[0],
                    kind="mcp",
                    render=render_json_mcp,
                    unrender=strip_json_mcp,
                )
            )
            actions.append(
                FileAction(
                    path=self._instructions_path(scope, project_root),
                    kind="instructions",
                    render=upsert_instructions,
                    unrender=remove_instructions,
                )
            )
        if seed_permissions:

    rendered: list[tuple[Path, str]] = []

        except InstallError as exc:

    """Write previously rendered ``(path, content)`` pairs. Returns paths."""
    written: list[Path] = []

    """Feed each action's pure render through the write system. Returns paths."""
    return write_rendered(render_plan(plan, write_system), write_system)


def apply_uninstall(plan: list[FileAction], write_system: WriteSystem) -> list[Path]:
    """Run each action's ``unrender`` in reverse: strip archy or delete the file.

    A file that does not exist is skipped (uninstall is idempotent). When
    ``unrender`` returns ``None`` the file is removed; otherwise the stripped
    content is written back. Returns the paths actually touched.

"""Orchestration for `archy install`: detect, select targets, apply plans.

CLI-agnostic on purpose. The Click command in ``archy.cli`` parses flags and
formats output; everything here returns structured results so the same logic is
driven directly by unit tests without going through ``CliRunner``.

archy:owns        AdapterResult, ConfigPreview, Detection, InstallResult, detect_all,
                  plan_for, preview_config, print_config, resolve_targets, run_install,
                  run_uninstall

                  resolve_targets -> archy.cli, archy.install,
                  run_install -> archy.cli, archy.install, run_uninstall -> archy.cli,
                  archy.install
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable
from pathlib import Path

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

from archy.install.base import (
    AgentAdapter,
    FileAction,
    Scope,
    apply_plan,
    apply_uninstall,
    remove_instructions,
    render_plan,
    write_rendered,
)
from archy.install.merge import denied_archy_permission_patterns
from archy.install.registry import all_adapters, get_adapter
from archy.install.writer import (
    DryRunWriteSystem,
    InstallError,
    RealWriteSystem,
    WriteSystem,
)

# Named so callers and tests never depend on the raw "auto"/"all" string literals.
TARGET_AUTO = "auto"
TARGET_ALL = "all"


class Detection(BaseModel):
    """Whether one adapter's client was found on this machine."""

    # arbitrary_types_allowed: `adapter` is an AgentAdapter instance (an ABC),
    # not a pydantic-native type.
    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, arbitrary_types_allowed=True)

    adapter: AgentAdapter
    detected: bool


class AdapterResult(BaseModel):
    """The files one adapter wrote during an install."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    adapter_id: str
    written: tuple[Path, ...] = ()
    notes: tuple[str, ...] = ()


class InstallResult(BaseModel):
    """All files written across the adapters in one install run."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    results: tuple[AdapterResult, ...] = ()

    def all_paths(self) -> list[Path]:
        return [p for r in self.results for p in r.written]

    def all_notes(self) -> list[str]:
        return [n for r in self.results for n in r.notes]


def detect_all() -> list[Detection]:
    """Probe every registered adapter. Order matches the registry."""
    return [Detection(adapter=a, detected=a.detect()) for a in all_adapters()]


def resolve_targets(target: str) -> list[AgentAdapter]:
    """Map a ``--target`` value to the adapters to act on.

    - ``auto``  -> only adapters that detect their client on this machine.
    - ``all``   -> every registered adapter, detected or not.
    - ``a,b,c`` -> exactly those adapter ids (detection ignored; explicit intent).

    Raises :class:`InstallError` for an unknown id or an empty ``auto`` result.
    """
    spec = target.strip().lower()
    if spec == TARGET_ALL:
        return list(all_adapters())
    if spec == TARGET_AUTO:
        detected = [d.adapter for d in detect_all() if d.detected]
        if not detected:
            raise InstallError(
                "No supported agent clients detected. Pass --target=<id> "
                "explicitly or --target=all. Known agents: "
                + ", ".join(a.id for a in all_adapters())
                + "."
            )
        return detected
    requested = [piece.strip() for piece in spec.split(",") if piece.strip()]
    if not requested:
        raise InstallError("Empty --target. Use auto, all, or a comma list of ids.")
    return [_known_adapter(adapter_id) for adapter_id in requested]


def _known_adapter(adapter_id: str) -> AgentAdapter:
    """`get_adapter`, but an unknown id is the user's input error, not a crash.

    The CLI turns `InstallError` into a clean `Error:` line (#337). `args[0]`
    rather than `str(exc)`, which would wrap the message in quotes.
    """
    try:
        return get_adapter(adapter_id)
    except KeyError as exc:
        raise InstallError(exc.args[0]) from exc


def plan_for(
    adapter: AgentAdapter,
    scope: Scope,
    *,
    project_root: Path | None,
    seed_permissions: bool,
    for_uninstall: bool = False,
) -> list[FileAction]:
    return adapter.plan(
        scope,
        project_root=project_root,
        seed_permissions=seed_permissions,
        for_uninstall=for_uninstall,
    )


def _run_for_adapters(
    adapters: list[AgentAdapter],
    scope: Scope,
    *,
    project_root: Path | None,
    seed_permissions: bool,
    write_system: WriteSystem | None,
    apply_fn: Callable[[list[FileAction], WriteSystem], list[Path]],
    for_uninstall: bool = False,
) -> InstallResult:
    """Plan each adapter and run ``apply_fn`` over it. Shared by install/uninstall.

    Install (#591) is two-phase: render every adapter first (collecting every
    ``InstallError``), write nothing if any failed, otherwise write all. Uninstall
    keeps the sequential ``apply_fn`` path so reverse order stays unchanged.
    """
    ws = write_system if write_system is not None else RealWriteSystem()
    if for_uninstall:
        results: list[AdapterResult] = []
        for adapter in adapters:
            plan = plan_for(
                adapter,
                scope,
                project_root=project_root,
                seed_permissions=seed_permissions,
                for_uninstall=True,
            )
            touched = apply_fn(plan, ws)
            results.append(
                AdapterResult(
                    adapter_id=adapter.id,
                    written=tuple(touched),
                    notes=(),
                )
            )
        return InstallResult(results=tuple(results))

    prepared: list[tuple[str, tuple[str, ...], list[tuple[Path, str]]]] = []
    errors: list[str] = []
    for adapter in adapters:
        plan = plan_for(
            adapter,
            scope,
            project_root=project_root,
            seed_permissions=seed_permissions,
            for_uninstall=False,
        )
        notes: list[str] = []
        for action in plan:
            if action.kind != "permissions":
                continue
            skipped = denied_archy_permission_patterns(ws.read_text(action.path))
            if skipped:
                notes.append("left denied (not added to allow): " + ", ".join(skipped))
        try:
            pairs = render_plan(plan, ws)
        except InstallError as exc:
            errors.append(f"{adapter.id}: {exc}")
            continue
        prepared.append((adapter.id, tuple(notes), pairs))

    if errors:
        raise InstallError("; ".join(errors))

    results = []
    for adapter_id, adapter_notes, pairs in prepared:
        touched = write_rendered(pairs, ws)
        results.append(
            AdapterResult(
                adapter_id=adapter_id,
                written=tuple(touched),
                notes=adapter_notes,
            )
        )
    return InstallResult(results=tuple(results))


def run_install(
    adapters: list[AgentAdapter],
    scope: Scope,
    *,
    project_root: Path | None = None,
    seed_permissions: bool = True,
    write_system: WriteSystem | None = None,
) -> InstallResult:
    """Apply each adapter's plan through ``write_system`` (real by default)."""
    return _run_for_adapters(
        adapters,
        scope,
        project_root=project_root,
        seed_permissions=seed_permissions,
        write_system=write_system,
        apply_fn=apply_plan,
    )


def run_uninstall(
    adapters: list[AgentAdapter],
    scope: Scope,
    *,
    project_root: Path | None = None,
    seed_permissions: bool = True,
    write_system: WriteSystem | None = None,
) -> InstallResult:
    """Reverse each adapter's plan: strip archy from configs, delete owned files.

    ``seed_permissions`` mirrors install so the Claude permission entries that
    install seeded are the ones uninstall removes (pass it through unchanged).
    Reports the paths touched (stripped or deleted) in the same result shape.
    """
    return _run_for_adapters(
        adapters,
        scope,
        project_root=project_root,
        seed_permissions=seed_permissions,
        write_system=write_system,
        apply_fn=apply_uninstall,
        for_uninstall=True,
    )


def print_config(
    adapter_id: str,
    scope: Scope,
    *,
    project_root: Path | None = None,
    seed_permissions: bool = True,
) -> list[tuple[Path, str]]:
    """Dry-run a single adapter: return the (path, rendered-content) it would write.

    Renders against the *real* current files (the dry-run system reads disk),
    so the preview reflects the actual merge result, not a fresh snippet.
    """
    previews = preview_config(
        adapter_id, scope, project_root=project_root, seed_permissions=seed_permissions
    )
    return [(p.path, p.rendered) for p in previews]


class ConfigPreview(BaseModel):
    """One file as install would leave it, with what to diff it against.

    ``without_archy`` is ``unrender(rendered)``: the user's content in the
    writer's own formatting, archy's part removed. Diffing it against
    ``rendered`` isolates archy's lines however the writer reformats the rest
    (#519). ``existing`` is the raw on-disk text, line endings kept, or ``None``
    when the file does not exist yet.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    path: Path
    existing: str | None
    rendered: str
    without_archy: str


def _without_archy(action: FileAction, rendered: str) -> str:
    """``unrender(rendered)``, or for a file archy owns, its non-archy text.

    An owned file's unrender deletes it (``None``). If install keeps user text
    outside a marker block (``upsert_instructions``), that text is the baseline,
    so it never prints; a file with no markers is archy's whole (``""``).
    """
    stripped = action.unrender(rendered)
    if stripped is not None:
        return stripped
    kept = remove_instructions(rendered)
    return "" if kept is None or kept == rendered else kept


def preview_config(
    adapter_id: str,
    scope: Scope,
    *,
    project_root: Path | None = None,
    seed_permissions: bool = True,
) -> list[ConfigPreview]:
    """Dry-run a single adapter and pair each rendered file with its baselines."""
    adapter = _known_adapter(adapter_id)
    ws = DryRunWriteSystem()
    plan = plan_for(adapter, scope, project_root=project_root, seed_permissions=seed_permissions)
    previews: list[ConfigPreview] = []
    for action in plan:
        existing_text = ws.read_text(action.path)
        try:
            rendered = action.render(existing_text)
        except InstallError as exc:
            msg = str(exc)
            if str(action.path) not in msg:
                raise InstallError(f"{action.path}: {msg}") from exc
            raise
        # Bytes, not read_text: universal newlines would hide a CRLF rewrite.
        existing = action.path.read_bytes().decode("utf-8") if action.path.exists() else None
        previews.append(
            ConfigPreview(
                path=action.path,
                existing=existing,
                rendered=rendered,
                without_archy=_without_archy(action, rendered),
            )
        )
    return previews

            for_uninstall=False,

        notes: list[str] = []
        for action in plan:
            if action.kind != "permissions":

            if skipped:
                notes.append("left denied (not added to allow): " + ", ".join(skipped))
        try:
            pairs = render_plan(plan, ws)
        except InstallError as exc:

        raise InstallError("; ".join(errors))

    scope: Scope,
    *,
    project_root: Path | None = None,
    seed_permissions: bool = True,
    write_system: WriteSystem | None = None,
) -> InstallResult:
    """Apply each adapter's plan through ``write_system`` (real by default)."""
    return _run_for_adapters(
        adapters,
        scope,
        project_root=project_root,
        seed_permissions=seed_permissions,
        write_system=write_system,
        apply_fn=apply_plan,
    )


def run_uninstall(
    adapters: list[AgentAdapter],
    scope: Scope,
    *,
    project_root: Path | None = None,
    seed_permissions: bool = True,
    write_system: WriteSystem | None = None,
) -> InstallResult:
    """Reverse each adapter's plan: strip archy from configs, delete owned files.

    ``seed_permissions`` mirrors install so the Claude permission entries that
    install seeded are the ones uninstall removes (pass it through unchanged).
    Reports the paths touched (stripped or deleted) in the same result shape.
    """
    return _run_for_adapters(
        adapters,

        project_root=project_root,
        seed_permissions=seed_permissions,
        write_system=write_system,

def print_config(
    adapter_id: str,
    scope: Scope,
    *,
    project_root: Path | None = None,
    seed_permissions: bool = True,
) -> list[tuple[Path, str]]:
    """Dry-run a single adapter: return the (path, rendered-content) it would write.

    Renders against the *real* current files (the dry-run system reads disk),
    so the preview reflects the actual merge result, not a fresh snippet.
    """
    previews = preview_config(
        adapter_id, scope, project_root=project_root, seed_permissions=seed_permissions
    )
    return [(p.path, p.rendered) for p in previews]


class ConfigPreview(BaseModel):
    """One file as install would leave it, with what to diff it against.

    ``without_archy`` is ``unrender(rendered)``: the user's content in the
    writer's own formatting, archy's part removed. Diffing it against
    ``rendered`` isolates archy's lines however the writer reformats the rest
    (#519). ``existing`` is the raw on-disk text, line endings kept, or ``None``
    when the file does not exist yet.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    path: Path
    existing: str | None
    rendered: str
    without_archy: str


def _without_archy(action: FileAction, rendered: str) -> str:
    """``unrender(rendered)``, or for a file archy owns, its non-archy text.

    An owned file's unrender deletes it (``None``). If install keeps user text
    outside a marker block (``upsert_instructions``), that text is the baseline,
    so it never prints; a file with no markers is archy's whole (``""``).
    """
    stripped = action.unrender(rendered)
    if stripped is not None:
        return stripped
    kept = remove_instructions(rendered)
    return "" if kept is None or kept == rendered else kept


def preview_config(
    adapter_id: str,
    scope: Scope,
    *,
    project_root: Path | None = None,
    seed_permissions: bool = True,
) -> list[ConfigPreview]:
    """Dry-run a single adapter and pair each rendered file with its baselines."""
    adapter = _known_adapter(adapter_id)
    ws = DryRunWriteSystem()
    plan = plan_for(adapter, scope, project_root=project_root, seed_permissions=seed_permissions)
    previews: list[ConfigPreview] = []
    for action in plan:
        existing_text = ws.read_text(action.path)
        try:
            rendered = action.render(existing_text)
        except InstallError as exc:
            msg = str(exc)
            if str(action.path) not in msg:
                raise InstallError(f"{action.path}: {msg}") from exc
            raise
        # Bytes, not read_text: universal newlines would hide a CRLF rewrite.
        existing = action.path.read_bytes().decode("utf-8") if action.path.exists() else None
        previews.append(
            ConfigPreview(
                path=action.path,
                existing=existing,
                rendered=rendered,
                without_archy=_without_archy(action, rendered),
            )
        )
    return previews

def _read_text(path: Path) -> str | None:
    try:
        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None
    except IsADirectoryError as error:
        raise InstallError(f"{path}: is a directory; archy will not edit it") from error
    except UnicodeDecodeError as error:
        raise InstallError(
            f"{path}: not valid UTF-8 ({error.reason} at byte {error.start}); "
            "archy will not edit it"
        ) from error
    except PermissionError as error:
        if path.is_dir():
            raise InstallError(f"{path}: is a directory; archy will not edit it") from error
        raise InstallError(f"{path}: cannot read ({error})") from error
    if text.startswith("\ufeff"):
        raise InstallError(f"{path}: starts with a UTF-8 BOM; archy will not edit it")
    return text


@dataclass
class RealWriteSystem:
    """Atomic, real-filesystem writes. Tracks written and removed paths."""

    written: list[Path] = field(default_factory=list)
    removed: list[Path] = field(default_factory=list)

    def read_text(self, path: Path) -> str | None:
        return _read_text(path)

    def exists(self, path: Path) -> bool:
        return path.exists()

    def remove(self, path: Path) -> None:
        try:
            path.unlink()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return
        self.removed.append(path)

    def write_text(self, path: Path, content: str) -> None:
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        # Write to a temp file in the same directory, then atomically rename.
        # Same-directory keeps the rename on one filesystem (cross-device
        # os.replace raises). Text mode with the default newline translation,
        # per the spec: we never hand-format line endings.
        fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=path.parent, prefix=f".{path.name}.", suffix=".tmp")
        tmp = Path(tmp_name)
        try:
            with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                fh.write(content)
            try:
                os.replace(tmp, path)
            except PermissionError as exc:
                # Windows holds an exclusive handle while an Electron client is
                # running, so the rename onto an open target fails. Surface a
                # clear instruction instead of retrying indefinitely.
                raise InstallError(
                    f"Could not write {path}: the file may be open in a running "
                    "client. Close the client and re-run `archy install`."
                ) from exc
        finally:
            if tmp.exists():
                tmp.unlink()
        self.written.append(path)


@dataclass
class DryRunWriteSystem:
    """Reads the real filesystem; captures writes and removals, performs neither."""

    records: list[WriteRecord] = field(default_factory=list)
    removed: list[Path] = field(default_factory=list)

    def read_text(self, path: Path) -> str | None:
        return _read_text(path)

    def exists(self, path: Path) -> bool:
        return path.exists()

    def write_text(self, path: Path, content: str) -> None:
        self.records.append(WriteRecord(path=path, content=content))

    def remove(self, path: Path) -> None:

    plan = ADAPTER.plan(Scope.GLOBAL, seed_permissions=True)

def test_plan_skips_mcp_when_plugin_installed(simulate_os):
    fake = simulate_os("linux")
    _write_plugin_manifest(fake.home, "archy")
    assert ADAPTER.plugin_installed() is True
    plan = ADAPTER.plan(Scope.GLOBAL, seed_permissions=True)
    # Plugin already registers MCP + ships the skill; only permissions remain.
    assert _kinds(plan) == ["permissions"]


def test_plan_for_uninstall_includes_mcp_even_when_plugin_installed(simulate_os):
    # Regression for #169: if the plugin is installed *after* a manual install,
    # the uninstall plan must still strip the MCP stanza + instructions a prior
    # install wrote, or they are orphaned. The reverse pass widens the plan
    # regardless of current plugin state.
    fake = simulate_os("linux")
    _write_plugin_manifest(fake.home, "archy")
    assert ADAPTER.plugin_installed() is True
    install_plan = ADAPTER.plan(Scope.GLOBAL, seed_permissions=True)
    uninstall_plan = ADAPTER.plan(Scope.GLOBAL, seed_permissions=True, for_uninstall=True)
    # Install still skips MCP + instructions (avoids #104 double-registration),
    # but uninstall removes them so the round-trip leaves no footprint.
    assert _kinds(install_plan) == ["permissions"]
    assert _kinds(uninstall_plan) == ["mcp", "instructions", "permissions"]


def test_plugin_detection_ignores_foreign_manifests(simulate_os):
    fake = simulate_os("linux")
    _write_plugin_manifest(fake.home, "other")

"""Layer 4: parse each emitted config back with the client's expected parser.

Catches "writer emits something the client would reject" without running the
client. Every assertion parses the bytes (JSON / TOML / YAML) rather than
string-matching, so cosmetic formatting changes don't cause false failures but a
structural break does.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys

import pytest
import yaml

from archy.install.base import Scope, apply_plan, permission_patterns
from archy.install.registry import get_adapter
from archy.install.writer import DryRunWriteSystem

if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):
    import tomllib
else:  # pragma: no cover
    import tomli as tomllib


def _emit(adapter_id: str, simulate_os, scope: Scope = Scope.GLOBAL) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Render an adapter on a faked Linux box; map basename -> content."""
    fake = simulate_os("linux")
    adapter = get_adapter(adapter_id)
    ws = DryRunWriteSystem()
    plan = adapter.plan(scope, project_root=fake.home / "proj", seed_permissions=True)
    apply_plan(plan, ws)
    return {r.path.name: r.content for r in ws.records}


def _assert_uvx_archy(entry: dict) -> None:
    assert entry["command"] == "uvx"
    assert entry["args"] == ["archy", "mcp"]


def test_claude_mcp_parses_as_json(simulate_os):
    files = _emit("claude", simulate_os)
    obj = json.loads(files[".claude.json"])
    _assert_uvx_archy(obj["mcpServers"]["archy"])


def test_claude_permissions_parses_with_all_tools(simulate_os):
    files = _emit("claude", simulate_os)
    obj = json.loads(files["settings.json"])
    assert set(permission_patterns()).issubset(set(obj["permissions"]["allow"]))


def test_cursor_mcp_parses_as_json(simulate_os):
    files = _emit("cursor", simulate_os)
    obj = json.loads(files["mcp.json"])
    _assert_uvx_archy(obj["mcpServers"]["archy"])

"""`archy install --print-config` shows archy's lines, not the user's file (#519).

Shared client configs such as ~/.claude.json hold the user's other MCP servers
and account data, so echoing the merged file printed their secrets. Every
fixture here plants a sentinel where a plausible implementation would leak it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json

from click.testing import CliRunner

from archy.cli import main
from archy.install.base import TOOL_NAMES

SENTINEL = "SENTINEL_SECRET"


def _seed(path, text: str):
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_bytes(text.encode("utf-8"))
    assert SENTINEL in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")  # the fixture carries it
    return path


def _claude_json(home, *, indent: int = 2, extra: str = "") -> None:
    """The other server's flat `apiKey` is its last line, so it sits directly
    above archy's inserted entry: any context line at all would carry it."""
    config = {
        "oauthAccount": {"emailAddress": "someone@example.com"},
        "mcpServers": {"other": {"command": "other-mcp", "apiKey": SENTINEL + extra}},
    }
    _seed(home / ".claude.json", json.dumps(config, indent=indent, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")


def _print_config(agent: str = "claude", *args: str) -> str:
    result = CliRunner().invoke(main, ["install", "--print-config", agent, *args])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    return result.output


def test_print_config_shows_archys_entry_and_not_the_neighbouring_secret(simulate_os):
    fake = simulate_os("linux")
    _claude_json(fake.home)

    out = _print_config()

    assert '"archy"' in out
    assert SENTINEL not in out
    assert "oauthAccount" not in out

    """4-space indent and a non-ASCII value: the writer rewrites both lines,
    which a plain on-disk diff printed twice. They are counted, not shown."""
    fake = simulate_os("linux")
    _claude_json(fake.home, indent=4, extra="-café")

    out = _print_config()

"""A global install writes no instruction block, and clears an old one (#560).

A client-wide instruction file (``~/.claude/CLAUDE.md``, ``~/.codex/AGENTS.md``)
is loaded in every project, Python or not, so archy's "call it before you edit"
block does not belong there. The block still goes into a project's own file on a
local install, so the guidance appears only where the user opted archy in.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from archy.install.base import Scope, instructions_block
from archy.install.runner import resolve_targets, run_install, run_uninstall
from archy.install.writer import RealWriteSystem

ADAPTERS = ["claude", "codex", "cursor", "opencode", "continue"]
# Where each adapter keeps its instruction file, relative to the (faked) home on
# linux, and whether archy owns the file outright (so retiring it deletes it).
GLOBAL_FILES = {
    "claude": (".claude/CLAUDE.md", False),
    "codex": (".codex/AGENTS.md", False),
    "opencode": (".config/opencode/AGENTS.md", False),
    "cursor": (".cursor/rules/archy.mdc", True),
    "continue": (".continue/rules/archy.md", True),
}
LOCAL_FILES = {
    "claude": "CLAUDE.md",
    "codex": "AGENTS.md",
    "opencode": "AGENTS.md",
    "cursor": ".cursor/rules/archy.mdc",
    "continue": ".continue/rules/archy.md",
}
USER_TEXT = b"# my notes\r\nkeep this exactly\r\n"  # CRLF: a rewrite would normalise it
OLD_BLOCK = instructions_block()


def _install(adapter_id: str, scope: Scope, project=None) -> None:
    run_install(
        resolve_targets(adapter_id),
        scope,
        project_root=project,
        write_system=RealWriteSystem(),
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("adapter_id", ADAPTERS)
def test_global_install_creates_no_instruction_file(adapter_id, simulate_os):
    fake = simulate_os("linux")
    rel, _owned = GLOBAL_FILES[adapter_id]

    _install(adapter_id, Scope.GLOBAL)

    assert not (fake.home / rel).exists()


@pytest.mark.parametrize("adapter_id", ["claude", "codex", "opencode"])
def test_global_install_leaves_a_users_own_file_byte_identical(adapter_id, simulate_os):
    fake = simulate_os("linux")
    path = fake.home / GLOBAL_FILES[adapter_id][0]
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_bytes(USER_TEXT)

    _install(adapter_id, Scope.GLOBAL)

    assert path.read_bytes() == USER_TEXT


@pytest.mark.parametrize("adapter_id", ["claude", "codex", "opencode"])
def test_global_install_removes_an_old_block_and_keeps_the_users_text(adapter_id, simulate_os):
    """Migration: a pre-#560 global install left the block next to the user's text."""
    fake = simulate_os("linux")
    path = fake.home / GLOBAL_FILES[adapter_id][0]
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    user = "# my notes\nkeep this exactly\n"
    path.write_text(f"{user}\n{OLD_BLOCK}", encoding="utf-8", newline="")
    assert "archy:begin" in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")  # the fixture has the block

    _install(adapter_id, Scope.GLOBAL)

    assert path.read_bytes() == user.encode("utf-8")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("adapter_id", ["claude", "codex", "opencode"])
def test_global_install_deletes_a_file_that_held_only_the_old_block(adapter_id, simulate_os):
    fake = simulate_os("linux")
    path = fake.home / GLOBAL_FILES[adapter_id][0]
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(OLD_BLOCK, encoding="utf-8", newline="")

    _install(adapter_id, Scope.GLOBAL)

    assert not path.exists()


@pytest.mark.parametrize("adapter_id", ["cursor", "continue"])
def test_global_install_deletes_a_rules_file_archy_owns(adapter_id, simulate_os):
    fake = simulate_os("linux")
    path = fake.home / GLOBAL_FILES[adapter_id][0]
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(OLD_BLOCK, encoding="utf-8", newline="")

    _install(adapter_id, Scope.GLOBAL)

    assert not path.exists()


def test_global_install_clears_the_old_block_even_when_the_claude_plugin_is_installed(
    simulate_os,
):
    fake = simulate_os("linux")
    manifest = fake.home / ".claude" / "plugins" / "archy" / ".claude-plugin" / "plugin.json"
    manifest.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    manifest.write_text('{"name": "archy"}', encoding="utf-8")
    path = fake.home / ".claude" / "CLAUDE.md"
    path.write_text(f"mine\n\n{OLD_BLOCK}", encoding="utf-8", newline="")

    _install("claude", Scope.GLOBAL)

    assert path.read_bytes() == b"mine\n"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("adapter_id", ADAPTERS)
def test_local_install_still_writes_the_block_into_the_project(adapter_id, simulate_os):
    """Guard: the fix must not pass by deleting the block everywhere."""
    fake = simulate_os("linux")
    project = fake.home / "proj"
    project.mkdir()

    _install(adapter_id, Scope.LOCAL, project)

    written = (project / LOCAL_FILES[adapter_id]).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert OLD_BLOCK in written


@pytest.mark.parametrize("adapter_id", ADAPTERS)
def test_a_local_install_and_uninstall_leaves_the_project_file_as_it_was(adapter_id, simulate_os):
    fake = simulate_os("linux")
    project = fake.home / "proj"
    project.mkdir()
    path = project / LOCAL_FILES[adapter_id]
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text("mine\n", encoding="utf-8", newline="")
    owned = adapter_id in {"cursor", "continue"}

    _install(adapter_id, Scope.LOCAL, project)
    run_uninstall(
        resolve_targets(adapter_id), Scope.LOCAL, project_root=project, write_system=RealWriteSystem()
    )

    # An archy-owned rules file is deleted on uninstall, user text and all (existing behaviour).
    assert path.exists() is not owned
    if not owned:
        assert path.read_bytes() == b"mine\n"

Code plugin. Per client it writes up to three things:

1. **An MCP server registration** pointing at `uvx archy mcp` (stdio). This is
   the functional wiring: the client launches the archy server on startup.
   Because it uses `uvx`, archy itself is fetched and run on demand from PyPI;
   nothing is copied onto your PATH.
2. **An instructions/rules file** with a short, marker-fenced block telling the
   agent *when* to call the tools (the snapshot -> impact -> diff loop).
3. **A permission allowlist (Claude Code only)** so you are not prompted to
   approve each of the 14 `mcp__archy__*` tools on first use.

It does **not** phone home, create an account, auto-update, or install the
`archy` CLI. (If you want the `archy` command on your PATH for direct CLI use,
that is a separate step: see [Installing the archy CLI](#installing-the-archy-cli-itself).)

## Install surfaces

There are three ways to wire archy in, plus the optional CLI install.

### 1. `archy install` (recommended, all clients)

Auto-detects which clients are present and configures each one. Idempotent, and
unrelated config in shared files is preserved. A shared rules file (`CLAUDE.md`,
`AGENTS.md`) with an `<!-- archy:begin -->` line that has no `<!-- archy:end -->`
of its own is refused and left as it is: `archy install` and `archy uninstall`
name the file and the line. Delete that marker, or add the end marker right after
archy's text and before anything of yours, then re-run. Install writes nothing
when it refuses; uninstall has already done the steps before the refusal, and the
re-run finishes the rest. Cursor's and Continue's rules files are archy's own:
install refuses the same way, and uninstall deletes them whatever they hold.

```bash
uvx archy install                              # detect, confirm, wire all
uvx archy install --target cursor,codex --yes  # non-interactive, specific clients
uvx archy install --target all --yes           # every known client, detected or not
| | `archy install` | Claude Code plugin |
|---|---|---|
| Clients | Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, opencode, Continue | Claude Code only |
| Acquisition | run a command in your shell | `/plugin marketplace add hslee16/archy` then `/plugin install archy@archy` |
| Seeds Claude `permissions.allow` | yes | no (loader limitation) |
| Ships the `archy` skill as a first-class skill | no (drops a `CLAUDE.md` block) | yes |
| Updates | you re-run / edit config | managed by Claude Code |
| Scriptable / CI | yes (`--yes`, `--target`, `--print-config`) | no |

`--location global` configures every project; `--location local` writes
project-scoped files under the current directory (or `--project-root`).

| Client | MCP config (global / local) | Instructions (global / local) | Permissions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `~/.claude.json` / `<project>/.mcp.json` | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` / `<project>/CLAUDE.md` | `~/.claude/settings.json` (or `<project>/.claude/settings.json`) |
| Cursor | `~/.cursor/mcp.json` / `<project>/.cursor/mcp.json` | `.cursor/rules/archy.mdc` (owned) | n/a |
| Codex CLI | `~/.codex/config.toml` / `<project>/.codex/config.toml` | `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` / `<project>/AGENTS.md` | n/a |
| opencode | `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` / `<project>/opencode.json` | `AGENTS.md` (alongside config) | n/a |
| Continue | `~/.continue/mcpServers/archy.yaml` / `<project>/.continue/...` (owned) | `.continue/rules/archy.md` (owned) | n/a |

On Windows the homedir-anchored paths resolve under `%USERPROFILE%`, and
opencode's global config lives under `%APPDATA%\opencode\`. Set `CODEX_HOME` and

cd /Users/hosanglee/archy; git commit -q -m "fix(install): a global install writes no instruction block, and clears an old one (#560)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && git push -q -u origin alee/global-install-no-instruction-block 2>&1 | tail -1; gh pr create --title "fix(install): a global install writes no instruction block, and clears an old one (#560)" --body "A client-wide instruction file (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, ...) is loaded in every project, so archy's block does not belong there.

- New \`instructions_action\` in \`install/base.py\`, used by all five adapters. Local installs write the block into the project's own file as before. Global installs write none.
- \`FileAction.retire\`: on a global install, strips an existing archy block (user text byte-identical; an archy-owned rules file is deleted; a file with no block is not touched or rewritten, so CRLF survives). Never creates a file. Runs even when the Claude plugin is installed.
- \`--print-config\` for global previews no instruction file; a malformed (unclosed) marker still refuses there.
- \`remove_instructions\` now drops the one blank separator line \`upsert_instructions\` inserts, so a strip is the exact inverse. Before, strip left \`mine\\n\\n\` where the file had been \`mine\\n\`, so local install then uninstall did not restore the file. This was needed for the migration to be byte-identical.
- Docs: INSTALL.md (what gets installed, path matrix), README, SAFETY.md (global write list 11 -> 6, plus the clean-up). Snapshots regenerated: pure deletions of the block from the 15 global snapshots.

Tests: new \`test_global_no_instructions.py\` (no file created, user file byte-identical incl. CRLF, migration, owned-file delete, plugin installed, local guard, local round trip). Mutation-verified, \`__pycache__\` cleared each time: unconditional global block (36 red), dropped local branch (28 red), reverted separator fix (7 red).

Makes no claim that removing the block saves tokens or improves agents; nothing measured it.

Closes #560
